title: Tenant-scoped MCP tool server with an audit log
area: Agentic apps on the platform: MCP, scopes, audit
scenario: Lumenfold's sales assistant needs tools over Keystone. The hackathon prototype of keystone-mcp searches every business unit, assigns leads directly and logs nothing. Turn it into the production tool surface: four task-level tools, identity from a signed delegation token, scope checks, idempotent writes, approval instead of assignment, and an append-only audit entry for every call.
task: Verify the delegation token (HMAC, expiry, claims) when the session starts
Scope every read and write to the delegated user's tenant; other tenants' ids are not found
crm.write for writes; log_activity idempotent per key; propose_lead_assignment starts an approval and never assigns
Audit every call (agent, on-behalf-of, tenant, tool, args hash, outcome, trace id), including denials
Tool descriptions written for a model; record content marked untrusted
acceptance: Two users in two tenants each see only their own data through a real MCP client session
No tool schema has a tenant, user or agent argument
Scope denials and not-found results are tool errors and are audited
Proposals are idempotent, start one approval and leave the lead unassigned

practices.label: Week 1 Fri - shared core: tool calling, MCP, LLM security
Week 6 Thu - workflow primitives for product teams and agents
